$schema: one entry per logical Garmin Connect operation this project depends on. method+path from live probing or from decompiling the Garmin Connect Android client (v5.29, 2026-09). lastVerified is when the status below was actually observed. observedStatus is what came back, not what is hoped for.

auth.notes: CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-09-16. This answers design.md Open Question 1: a CAS service ticket IS exchangeable for a long-lived OAuth1 token, and with login-url=https://connect.garmin.com/modern -- NOT only garth's https://sso.garmin.com/sso/embed, which was the open worry when this entry was first added. Evidence: a real device completed sign-in and immediately performed authenticated reads (dailyFoodLog returned today's calories), which is impossible without a valid OAuth1 token stored by this route. Status recorded as 200 by inference from that success rather than from a logged response line; correct it if a real capture ever says otherwise. The three defects that made the earlier attempt fail were: login-url naming a different CAS service than the ticket was minted for, and an OAuth1 signature that both kept the query string on the base string URI and signed an empty oauth_token. Response parses as a query-string body carrying oauth_token/oauth_token_secret, as modelled on garth -- that shape is now confirmed too, since a wrong guess would have thrown malformedExchangeResponse instead of authenticating.

OAuth1-signed request, returns an OAuth2 access token valid ~24h (observed expires_in=88227s). This is the only working auth path since Garmin blocked scripted SSO login behind Cloudflare in March 2026 -- see garth's deprecation. Verified by live use in tools/lib/garmin-auth.mjs.

read.notes: Legacy/general daily summary. Exposes consumedKilocalories, remainingKilocalories, activeKilocalories, bmrKilocalories -- but consumedKilocalories was observed null even on a date where nutrition-service/food/logs/{date} showed real logged food. Do not treat this as the nutrition source of truth; it appears to be a separate, disconnected field. Kept only as a control route to confirm auth is alive.

FatSecret- and Garmin-sourced results. Czech terms return results. Parameter name was discovered from a 400 error body naming 'searchFood.arg0.searchExpression'. Response: { results: [{ type, foodMetaData: { foodId, foodName, foodType, source (FATSECRET|GARMIN), regionCode, languageCode }, nutritionContents: [{ servingId, servingUnit, numberOfUnits, calories, carbs, protein, fat, fiber, sugar, saturatedFat, monounsaturatedFat, polyunsaturatedFat, cholesterol, sodium, potassium, vitaminA, vitaminC, calcium, iron, unitHasServing }], isFavorite, isRecent, servingQty, logTimestamp }], moreDataAvailable }. regionCode/languageCode are response-only, not accepted as query filters (tried, got 400).
Confirmed param name via 400 body: 'getAutocompleteSuggestions.arg0' searchExpression query parameter must be provided -- same param name as foodSearch. Not yet tested with a real term.

Route confirmed to exist: no-param request returns 400 naming 'getFoodByBarCode.arg1' and 'barCode query parameter must be provided'. A real-looking EAN-13 (8594001020010) returned 404, which is 'no product for this barcode', not 'route missing' -- distinguishable because the no-param case was 400, not 404. Needs a barcode known to exist in the DB to confirm the success payload shape.

GET returned 404 (expected -- this is POST-shaped, per the write-request nature of an image upload). Not exercised as POST. Out of scope for this project's MVP -- app's own VisionKit barcode scan covers the barcode case, and barcode scanning itself was deprioritized 2026-09-14 (see garmin-food-log-contract.md) after the owner found Garmin's own native scanner doesn't recognize Czech barcodes. AI photo recognition is lower priority still.

THE CORRECT read route -- plural 'logs', not 'log'. The vault's scripts/lib/garmin.mjs calls the singular '/nutrition-service/food/log/date/{date}', which 404s; that one-letter difference is why getNutritionLog() has silently returned null since it was written. Confirmed live with real data present on this account for 2026-09-14. Response top level: { mealDate, dayStartTime, dayEndTime, dailyViewType, dailyNutritionGoals: { calories, adjustedCalories, carbs, adjustedCarbs, fat, adjustedFat, protein, adjustedProtein }, dailyNutritionContent: { calories, carbs, fat, protein, caloriesPercentage }, mealDetails: [{ meal: { mealId, mealIndex, mealName (BREAKFAST/...), displayOrder, startTime, endTime, goals, editable, translated }, mealNutritionContent, mealNutritionGoals, loggedFoods: [{ id, logId, logTimestamp, logSource (GCM observed), logCategory (REGULAR_LOG observed), servingQty, foodMetaData, nutritionContent, isFavorite, mealId, customMealId, mealTime, foodInactive, type }] }], loggedFoodsWithServingSizes: [...] }. dayStartTime/dayEndTime were 04:00:00/17:00:00 on the observed day -- the nutrition 'day' window is configurable and is NOT simple local midnight-to-midnight; account for this when reading 'today'.

Shape inspected 2026-09-16: { meals: [{ mealId (number, a per-date meal INSTANCE id), mealName (BREAKFAST|LUNCH|DINNER|SNACKS), startTime, endTime }], dailyTimelineStartTime, dailyTimelineEndTime, dailyViewType }. BREAKFAST/LUNCH/DINNER carry an HH:mm:ss window; SNACKS carries none. Returned whether or not anything is logged. This is where createFoodLogEntry gets its mealId, which is why GarminClient.createFoodLogEntry calls it first.

Confirmed live via probe-garmin-nutrition.mjs. Response shape not yet inspected in detail -- a strong candidate for the food-catalog capability's quick-pick/recents list, straight from Garmin rather than locally derived.

Route exists but GET is not the right method (405 Method Not Allowed) -- unlike every other 'list' route here, this one likely requires POST with a body, or the list lives under a different path (e.g. plain /nutrition-service/favorite). Needs a follow-up probe, not a dead end. Sibling write routes: POST /nutrition-service/favorite/food, DELETE /nutrition-service/favorite/food/{foodId}, GET/POST /nutrition-service/favorite/meal.
Confirmed live via probe-garmin-nutrition.mjs. Needed to build a valid custom-food creation payload -- see food-catalog capability D4.

Shape: { weightChangeType (LOSS observed), targetDate, weightChangeRate, activeDailyCalories, userDefinedActiveCalories, calorieGoal, macroGoals: { carbs, fat, protein }, autoCalorieAdjustment, regionCode, languageCode, dailyTimelineStartTime, dailyTimelineEndTime, startingWeight, targetWeightGoal, effectiveDate, nutritionStatus (ACTIVE observed) }. macroGoals are GRAMS: they equalled the daily log's base (non-adjusted) goals exactly on the probed day. Read-only in this app (GarminClient.nutritionSettings); garmin_mcp writes it with PUT to the same path, which this project does not use.

Confirmed live via probe-garmin-nutrition.mjs. Candidate for a cheaper 'just the running total' read than the full dailyFoodLog payload -- worth inspecting its response shape before defaulting every widget refresh to the heavier route.

Confirmed live with a real date range. Accepts a MULTI-DAY range in one call -- more efficient than calling dailyFoodLog once per day for a trend view. Response: { startDate, endDate, caloriesBurned, mealNutritionContents: [], dailyNutritionContents: [{ mealDate, nutritionContent?: { calories, carbs, fat, protein, otherCalories, caloriesPercentage }, nutritionGoals?: { calories, adjustedCalories, carbs, adjustedCarbs, fat, adjustedFat, protein, adjustedProtein } }], averageNutritionContents: {} }. Days with no logged food omit nutritionContent/nutritionGoals entirely (bare { mealDate }) rather than returning zeros -- treat a missing key as 'nothing logged', not an error. nutritionGoals values cross-checked exactly against dailyFoodLog's dailyNutritionGoals for the same day (2300/3128/316/430/64/87/115/156) -- consistent between routes. Sibling: /nutrition-service/calorie/summary/weekly, same param shape presumed, not tested.

The profile the Garmin Connect app shows: displayName, fullName, userName, location, profileImageUrlSmall/Medium/Large, plus many visibility flags and Garmin's own userLevel/userPoint (unrelated to this app's XP and deliberately not shown). GarminClient.socialProfile decodes only the name, location and photo fields. Same route python-garminconnect uses for get_full_name.

write.notes: CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-09-16: a real device logged a FATSECRET food to DINNER and it read back once, filed under the right meal, with logSource GCW, logCategory REGULAR_LOG, mealTime equal to the meal window start, servingQty as sent, and regionCode US. Status is recorded as 200 because the write succeeded, not from a logged response line. Body { mealDate, foodLogItems: [{ logTimestamp, logSource, logCategory, mealTime, action: ADD, mealId, foodId, servingId, source: GARMIN|FATSECRET, regionCode, languageCode, servingQty }] } -- taken from garmin_mcp (Taxuspt/garmin_mcp, log_food_to_meal), which writes to this route in its own live end-to-end tests. Supersedes the earlier dex-string inference (a flat POST of date/mealType/foodId/servingId/numberOfUnits), which was wrong on method, envelope, meal (name vs per-date mealId), quantity field (numberOfUnits vs servingQty) and the missing source -- and is what the app sent when its first real write on a device failed on 2026-09-16 (status not captured; the failure was swallowed at the time). Full field notes in docs/garmin-food-log-contract.md. The first successful write from this project is still pending; tools/garmin-write-probe.mjs makes it from Windows.

Per garmin_mcp (log_food): PUT with { mealDate, quickAddItems: [{ name, logId: null, logTimestamp, logSource, logCategory: QUICK_ADD, mealTime, mealId, action: ADD, calories, carbs, protein, fat }] } -- logs a named entry by macros alone, no foodId. The earlier note here (DTO FoodLogQuickAddRequestDTO, guessed to take a favorite foodId) came from dex strings and is superseded. Not used by this project.
DTOs BulkFoodLogRequestDTO(action=...) and BulkFoodLogItemDTO(logId=...) found in decompiled client. Out of scope for MVP -- single-entry create covers this project's use case.

write.observedStatus: modelled on a live-tested client, not yet exercised by this project
write.notes: Per garmin_mcp (delete_food_log): the date is part of the PATH, which the earlier dex-string inference omitted; body { logIds: [...] }, each a 32-char hex logId from a read entry (not a foodId). Used by Reconciliation to remove a detected duplicate -- which, now that writes can succeed, is only allowed for entries logged no earlier than the local entry was queued (Reconciliation.couldBeThisAppsDelivery), so an identical entry made in the official app is never mistaken for one.

write.notes: String literal found in decompiled client. Sibling: PUT/DELETE /nutrition-service/customFood/{customFoodUuid}. Real device attempt (2026-09-21) returned 400 BadRequestException: 'custom food nutrition information is missing for the provided food id with region code and language code' -- the original request body had no regionCode/languageCode fields at all. Added both, using the same confirmed constants (US/en) FoodLogWriteBody's proven write contract already sends. Still genuinely unconfirmed whether this fully fixes it (no device retry has been reported back yet) -- the field NAMES/nesting remain a guess, just one now directly motivated by the exact error text rather than blind inference.
